subject: chemistry
title: Dynamic Drift: Kc and Reversible Reactions
welcome_lead: Master the equilibrium constant Kc in reversible reactions.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Kc, equilibrium and reversible reactions.
final_note: You balanced the forward and backward currents of reaction.

concepts.def: Same form as Kc, at any moment.
Species in different phases; solids omitted.

walkthroughs.body_html:
For aA + bB <-> cC + dD: Kc = [C]^c [D]^d / [A]^a [B]^b. Use equilibrium concentrations only.

Pure solids and liquids have constant activities and do not appear, e.g. CaCO3 <-> CaO(s) + CO2(g) gives Kc = [CO2].

List initial moles, change (in stoichiometric ratio), equilibrium values. Divide by volume to get concentrations.

Substitute into Kc and solve for unknown. Quadratic may be needed; small-x approximation valid when Kc is very small.

walkthroughs.h2: Predicting direction with Q vs Kc
walkthroughs.body_html:
If Q < Kc: net forward reaction. Q > Kc: net reverse. Q = Kc: at equilibrium.

Useful when mixing arbitrary amounts to predict shift without solving the full ICE.

mcqs.q: What are the units of Kc for a reaction?
options: Kc always has units of mol dm^-3.
They depend on Δn (the difference between moles of gaseous/aqueous products and reactants) — Kc can be dimensionless or have units like mol dm^-3.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.

mcqs.q: Does adding a catalyst change the value of Kc?
options: A catalyst increases Kc by favouring product formation.
A catalyst decreases Kc by stabilising the reactants.
No — a catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so Kc is unchanged.

mcqs.q: At dynamic equilibrium, what is happening to the reactions?
options: Both reactions stop because the system has reached balance.
Forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; concentrations remain constant.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.
